name: Score evidence against benchmark on the 5-point rubric

llm.prompt_template:
Score this piece of evidence against the benchmark on a 5-point scale.

Evidence (verbatim quote from a {kind} source):
"{quote}"

Benchmark ({kind}):
{benchmark_text}

Policy query: {query_id}{jurisdiction_clause}

Rubric (Table 6 of the LobbyMap methodology, applied verbatim):
  +2  Strongly supporting
        science_based:     "Detailed position aligned with IPCC analysis."
        government_policy: "Strong support for the policy and/or advocacy
                            that would strengthen the policy further."
  +1  Supporting
        science_based:     "Broad alignment with IPCC analysis."
        government_policy: "General or high-level support for the policy."
   0  No position / Mixed
        science_based:     "Unclear if position is aligned with IPCC analysis."
        government_policy: "Unclear if position is supportive of the policy."
  -1  Not supporting
        science_based:     "Position appears misaligned with IPCC analysis."
        government_policy: "Unsupportive of the policy and/or supportive
                            with caveats that would weaken the proposal."
  -2  Opposing
        science_based:     "Position contradicts IPCC analysis."
        government_policy: "Opposes the policy."

For government_policy benchmarks: only apply if all four §4.4 conditions
hold (specific clearly-communicated proposal from a mandated government
body; close to original policy intent; jurisdiction still in Paris;
proposal not at odds with IPCC). If any condition fails, decline to
score against this benchmark and return precedence_failure: true.

Return JSON:
  {{"score": -2|-1|0|1|2,
    "reasoning": "...one paragraph linking quote to rubric tier...",
    "precedence_failure": false}}

+2.label: Strongly supporting
+2.science_based: Detailed position that is aligned with IPCC analysis
+2.government_policy: Strong support for the policy and/or advocacy that would strengthen the policy further

+1.label: Supporting
+1.government_policy: General or high-level support for the policy

0.label: No position / Mixed position
0.science_based: Unclear if position is aligned with IPCC analysis
0.government_policy: Unclear if position is supportive of the policy

-1.label: Not supporting
-1.science_based: Position appears misaligned with IPCC analysis
-1.government_policy: Unsupportive of the policy and/or with major weakening caveats

compiler_notes: Rubric pulled verbatim from Table 6. The dual-column structure (science_ based + government_policy) is preserved so the prompt shows the LLM the exact tier descriptions for each benchmark kind.

§4.4 precedence rule (when government_policy can override science_based) is encoded inside the prompt rather than in upstream join logic, because three of the four conditions require reading the evidence text.
Multiple rows per evidence_id are normal — one per applicable benchmark. Downstream stages collapse this in cell aggregation.

eval.notes:
Use prior LobbyMap-coded evidence as ground truth. Even a few hundred
examples per query is enough to detect calibration drift across model
versions or prompt edits.
